Expectation1: Look out for each other's safety and well-being
Situation1: One sibling is about to cross the street without looking for oncoming traffic.
Situation2: Your friend has misunderstood the tone of your text message and replied sounding hurt. You need to call them right now to explain.
Story: I was walking home from school with my younger brother when my phone buzzed. It was a message from my best friend, Mia. She’d misunderstood my earlier text and now sounded really upset, her words sharp and distant. My heart dropped—I knew I had to call her right away to clear things up before things got worse. As I fumbled for my phone, I glanced up and saw my brother, distracted and laughing, stepping off the curb without looking. Cars were coming fast. I felt a surge of panic. I was supposed to keep him safe, to always watch out for him. But Mia needed me too, and I could hear the hurt in her message. My mind raced, torn between shouting for my brother to stop and dialing Mia’s number to fix things before she shut me out. Both needed me in this exact moment, and I could feel the weight of their expectations pressing down, my heart pounding as I stood frozen on the sidewalk.
